subject.title: feat(secrets): expose degraded owners to operators

question: Should operator status permanently expose `secrets.degraded[]` with public owner identifiers, redacted reasons, config paths, cold/stale state, and retry guidance while retaining the legacy cold-owner field?
rationale: This creates a durable secrets-runtime protocol surface and exposes operational metadata across generated clients; code review can validate mechanics but cannot choose the permanent operator visibility and compatibility boundary.

options.title: Approve after corrections
options.body: Approve the additive contract after both state-lifecycle defects are fixed, live behavior is demonstrated, and the security owner confirms the exposed metadata boundary.

options.title: Keep legacy status only
options.body: Do not add the nested RPC contract and limit improved guidance to existing status and doctor projections until a narrower protocol design is approved.

options.title: Narrow exposed metadata
options.body: Approve a reduced contract that omits fields the security owner considers too sensitive or too costly to support permanently.

recommendation.title: Approve after corrections
recommendation.body: Approve the additive contract after both state-lifecycle defects are fixed, live behavior is demonstrated, and the security owner confirms the exposed metadata boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly routes secrets-runtime and protocol exposure to this CODEOWNER team, and the unresolved choice concerns operator-visible secret metadata.
